section_summary: This section completes a SCAP register of Japanese ship-radio licenses, listing additions, deletions, changes, call signs, operating agencies, frequencies, powers, and emission types for vessels throughout Japan. It then begins a separate directory of Japanese radio stations, defining technical terms and limitations, giving standard-frequency and time-signal schedules, and listing land stations geographically with their services, frequencies, call signs, and coordinates. The geographical directory covers Niigata through Kanagawa prefectures in the pages provided and continues beyond this section.

subfiles.title: SCAP Ship Radio Register: Additions, Deletions, Changes, and Call-Sign Amendments
subfiles.about: Register pages record additions, deletions, and changes to Japanese vessel radio licenses and call signs.
subfiles.summary: The document continues a regional register of Japanese ships, giving SCAP registration numbers, registry ports, tonnage, operational agencies, call signs, authorized frequencies, power changes, and emission types. Separate parts identify deleted and changed registrations and then list call-sign additions, deletions, and transfers. Entries cover fishing boats, cargo vessels, tankers, training ships, and Maritime Safety Bureau guard boats throughout Japan; page 759 is a blank separator following the final amendment table.

subfiles.title: Japanese Radio Stations: Definitions, Technical Limitations, Time Signals, and Geographical List
subfiles.about: A national directory explains Japanese radio-allocation terminology and begins a geographically organized register of land stations.
subfiles.summary: The directory opens with its contents, definitions of frequency, emission, power, station classes, services, and channel terminology, followed by technical tolerances and operating limitations. It provides schedules and signal charts for standard-frequency and time transmissions from the Tokyo-area JJY, JJC, and JCS stations, plus service abbreviations. The geographical register then lists stations by prefecture, with SCAP numbers, frequencies, call signs, power, emission class, service, limitations, locations, and coordinates, covering Niigata through Kanagawa in this section.
